name: city-hall-kit
summary:
Wrote `plan.md`: all four modules share one column section. Fluted quartz-pillar Doric columns, spaced 8 apart, stand 4 blocks in front of a recessed diorite wall of tall windows, over a rusticated base, with a triglyph entablature, attic and balustrade. The portico and corner pavilion stand 1 block forward, and wing bays tile with no visible seam.
The portico carries six columns plus flanking pairs, three arched doorways reached by slab steps, and a pediment with relief.
Plot 0 sets a 46-across drum (16 paired columns, 8 tall windows, stepped attic) on the square pavilion. On it goes a lead-grey tuff dome with 16 andesite ribs and a gold band, then a columned lantern and gold cupola and finial to y 125. Gold appears only there, so the gilded dome over the colonnade is what makes it read as City Hall. Nothing was built or rendered, so none of this has been checked yet. A Beaux-Arts palace in four modules sharing one wing section: a rusticated diorite base, giant 2x2 quartz_pillar Doric columns standing 4 in front of a recessed wall of tall grey-glass windows, a triglyph entablature, an attic and a diorite balustrade, the pattern tiling seamlessly on a 4-block grid.
The portico adds three arched doorways with slab steps, six columns plus flanking pairs and a calcite pediment carrying quartz relief. The corner pavilion turns the corner on pilastered antas under a taller panelled attic.
Plot 0 stacks the same order on four faces, a drum ringed by 16 paired columns, a 2-thick polished_tuff dome (16 andesite ribs, gold band, ring and cartouches, glowstone in the inner shell), and a columned gold-cupola lantern to y 125. The design is written but not yet built or rendered. (13 of 14 parts finished)
